source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Quadratic variation of an Itô row up to a fixed dyadic time. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Let X be the sum of a drift with almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on [0,T] and a finite row of completed scalar Itô integrals. The integrals are driven by the coordinates of a standard vector Brownian motion relative to the given filtration and measure. For a fixed coarse dyadic time τ, the prefix sums of squared fine-grid increments of X converge in measure to the integrated squared row norm up to τ.

The underlying measure is finite and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. The Euclidean-valued standard Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
Each coordinate integrand is progressive and square-integrable for the product of the horizon time measure and the underlying measure. The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality.
The horizon T is positive. At each deterministic time t≤T, the drift Aₜ is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Almost every drift path is continuous and has bounded variation on [0,T].
The cutoff τ is any fixed grid point of a specified coarse dyadic grid on [0,T].

\sum_{i:\ t_{i+1}\le\tau}(X_{t_{i+1}}-X_{t_i})^2\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mu}\sum_{j}\int_{[0,\tau]}\eta_j(s)^2\,ds,\qquad X_t=A_t+\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_j(s)\,dB^j_s.

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
      filtration μ)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
  (η : J → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
  (A : NNReal → Ω → ℝ) (hAmeas : ∀ t ≤ T, MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (A t) μ)
  (hA : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T) ∧ BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T))
  (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) :
  have τ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.regularGridTimes
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) k;
  have X := fun t ω =>
    A t ω +
      ∑ j,
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess (η j) hT ⋯ hUsual t
          ω;
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
    (fun n ω =>
      have t :=
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.regularGridTimes
          (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.dyadicMesh T n)
          (2 ^ n);
      ∑ i, if t i.succ ≤ τ then (X (t i.succ) ω - X (t i.castSucc) ω) ^ 2 else 0)
    Filter.atTop fun ω =>
    ∑ j,
      ∫ (s : NNReal) in Set.Iic τ,
        (η j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let J be finite with decidable equality, Omega a measurable space with finite measure mu, F a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, T>0, and B an R^J-valued standard Brownian motion with F. A vector standard Brownian motion with filtration F here starts at zero for every sample, has jointly independent increments over each finite family of disjoint half-open intervals, has centered Gaussian increment projections with variance (t-s)*||ell||^2 for every continuous linear functional ell and s<t, has almost surely continuous paths, is strongly F-adapted, and has each increment from s to t independent of F_s when s<=t. Usual conditions mean every null subset of Omega belongs to every F_t, and F is right-continuous. Write lambda_H for real Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,H] and transported to NNReal. A progressive L2 integrand on horizon H is a real strongly F-progressive process belonging to L2(mu product lambda_H), after ordering its arguments as (omega,t). Write I^H_j(h)(t) for its specified completed Ito integral against the coordinate B_j(t,omega) of B. This is the canonical elementary-approximation path limit, patched to zero on its exceptional null set and held constant after H. Let eta_j, j in J, be progressive L2 integrands on [0,T]. Let A:NNReal x Omega->R have an mu-almost-everywhere strongly measurable slice at every t<=T and, for mu-almost every omega, a continuous path of bounded variation on [0,T]. Fix m in N and k in {0,...,2^m}, and put tau=k*T/2^m. Define X(t,omega)=A(t,omega)+sum_j I^T_j(eta_j)(t,omega). For n in N put t_i^n=i*T/2^n. Then
sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} 1_{t_{i+1}^n<=tau}*(X(t_{i+1}^n,omega)-X(t_i^n,omega))^2
converges in mu-measure to sum_j integral_{[0,T] intersect [0,tau]} eta_j(s,omega)^2 ds as n tends to infinity. The process X is not stopped. The sum includes exactly cells whose right endpoint is at most the fixed dyadic tau; its definition applies for every n, including n<m. No adaptedness of A is assumed.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.DyadicCutoffIncrements
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoFiniteVariationQV

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoDyadicPrefixQV

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 StoppingTime ElementaryItoIntegral
  SampledElementaryApproximation DyadicElementaryRefinement EuclideanBrownianCoordinates
  ItoIntegralProcess ItoFiniteVariationQV DyadicCutoffIncrements

/-- Quadratic variation along the prefix of the fine grid ending at a
fixed coarse dyadic cutoff. -/
theorem tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_prefix_sq_increments_of_ito_row
    {Ω J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : ℝ≥0}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration μ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
    (η : J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
    (A : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (hAmeas : ∀ t ≤ T, AEStronglyMeasurable (A t) μ)
    (hA : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A t ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A t ω) (Icc 0 T))
    (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ m + 1)) :
    let τ := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T m) (2 ^ m) k
    let X := fun t ω => A t ω + ∑ j : J,
      itoIntegralProcess (η j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω
    TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =>
      let t := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
      ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), if t i.succ ≤ τ then
        (X (t i.succ) ω - X (t i.castSucc) ω) ^ 2 else 0) atTop
      (fun ω => ∑ j : J, ∫ s in Iic τ, (η j).process s ω ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) := by
  intro τ X
  have hτ : τ ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone (Fin.le_last k)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T m)
  let S (t : ℝ≥0) := min τ t
  let A₀ (t : ℝ≥0) := A (S t)
  have hA₀ (t : ℝ≥0) (_ht : t ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A₀ t) μ :=
    hAmeas _ ((min_le_left τ t).trans hτ)
  have hmaps : MapsTo S (Icc 0 T) (Icc 0 T) := fun t _ =>
    ⟨bot_le, (min_le_left τ t).trans hτ⟩
  have hmono : Monotone S := fun _ _ ht => min_le_min_left τ ht
  have hcont : Continuous S := continuous_const.min continuous_id
  have hA₀path : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hA] with ω hω
    refine ⟨hω.1.comp hcont.continuousOn hmaps, ?_⟩
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top hω.2
      (eVariationOn.comp_le_of_monotoneOn (fun t => A t ω) S (hmono.monotoneOn _) hmaps)
  have h := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sq_increments_stopped_ito_add_boundedVariation
    hB hT hUsual η (fun _ => τ) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration τ) (fun _ => hτ)
    A₀ hA₀ hA₀path
  refine TendstoInMeasure.congr' ?_ EventuallyEq.rfl h
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop m] with n hn
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by
    simpa only [pow_two, X, A₀, S] using
      dyadic_sum_mul_stopped_increments_eq_prefix hT hn k (fun t => X t ω) (fun t => X t ω)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoDyadicPrefixQV

lesson.statement: Let X be the sum of a drift with almost surely continuous finite-variation paths on [0,T] and a finite row of completed scalar Itô integrals. The integrals are driven by the coordinates of a standard vector Brownian motion relative to the given filtration and measure. For a fixed coarse dyadic time τ, the prefix sums of squared fine-grid increments of X converge in measure to the integrated squared row norm up to τ.

Each coordinate integrand is progressive and square-integrable for the product of the horizon time measure and the underlying measure. The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality.

steps.title: Stop the drift by a monotone time change
steps.text: The map that clips time at τ is continuous, nondecreasing and maps the horizon into itself. Its composition with the drift preserves the path conditions and has almost-everywhere measurable evaluations at each time.
steps.lean:
intro τ X
  have hτ : τ ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT m) _).monotone (Fin.le_last k)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T m)
  let S (t : ℝ≥0) := min τ t
  let A₀ (t : ℝ≥0) := A (S t)
  have hA₀ (t : ℝ≥0) (_ht : t ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A₀ t) μ :=
    hAmeas _ ((min_le_left τ t).trans hτ)
  have hmaps : MapsTo S (Icc 0 T) (Icc 0 T) := fun t _ =>
    ⟨bot_le, (min_le_left τ t).trans hτ⟩
  have hmono : Monotone S := fun _ _ ht => min_le_min_left τ ht
  have hcont : Continuous S := continuous_const.min continuous_id
  have hA₀path : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) ∧
      BoundedVariationOn (fun t => A₀ t ω) (Icc 0 T) := by
    filter_upwards [hA] with ω hω
    refine ⟨hω.1.comp hcont.continuousOn hmaps, ?_⟩
    exact ne_top_of_le_ne_top hω.2
      (eVariationOn.comp_le_of_monotoneOn (fun t => A t ω) S (hmono.monotoneOn _) hmaps)

steps.title: Apply stopped quadratic variation
steps.text: The fixed time is a bounded stopping time. With the clipped drift, the existing stopped-row theorem gives convergence of the squared increments of the full stopped process to the restricted energy.
steps.lean:
have h := tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sq_increments_stopped_ito_add_boundedVariation
    hB hT hUsual η (fun _ => τ) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration τ) (fun _ => hτ)
    A₀ hA₀ hA₀path

steps.title: Replace stopped increments by the prefix
steps.text: Every sufficiently fine grid refines the chosen coarse grid. The deterministic cutoff identity with both paths equal to X gives exact equality of the two sums at those levels.
steps.lean:
refine TendstoInMeasure.congr' ?_ EventuallyEq.rfl h
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop m] with n hn
  exact Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by
    simpa only [pow_two, X, A₀, S] using
      dyadic_sum_mul_stopped_increments_eq_prefix hT hn k (fun t => X t ω) (fun t => X t ω)

lesson.lean_statement: The stopped-row construction uses the actual completed Itô process for each Brownian coordinate. The time integral is restricted to Iic τ under TimeMeasure.upTo T.
lesson.lean_proof: Clip the drift, apply the stopped-row limit at the deterministic stopping time and identify the sums on all refinements.
